description_en: Mūchẽ Āgama is located to the north of the Bahādur Śāha. The building can be accessed through a small door opening on the western boundary wall.The Āgama was located at the south of a small courtyard facing north. The main entry door on the ground floor can be reached by climbing up on to a raised plinth guarded by two small stone lions. The main carved door is flanked by two small blind windows on either sides. A small secondary entry door on the principal façade (the eastern end of the building) leads to a stairway. There were two three-foldpasukā jhyāḥon the first and second floor, both of which were salvaged after the earthquake.The historical name of the Āgama is Maṇichẽ, meaning a house located in the Maṇigala Ṭola. The wordmaṇichẽhas changed intomūchẽover the course of time. This building appears to be a normal residential building, however, this is in fact theāgãchẽof the Jośīs of Bakhumbāhāla and Kisis (Śreṣṭha) of Ombāhāla. The Rājopādhyāyas of the Svãtha Ṭola perform the daily ritual worship here. Manamāneśvarī, the lineage deity of Licchavi kings who was worshipped before Taleju was brought to the Valley, is also worshipped inside this shrine.The Āgama used to house a collection of the swords of kings. When a ruling king died, his sword was preserved here.Jośī(2065, 16-17) states that there were once more than 30 swords inside this Āgama. The three-storey building of the Āgamawas heavily damaged in the 2015 earthquake and now only the front wall of the ground floor remains. The main deity has been relocated to a neighboring house and various small images have been preserved in the Patan Museum.No historical record confirming the initial construction of the shrine is available. A Gaṇeśa statue located to the north-west was established in 1434 (NS 558). This provides grounds to assume that the Āgama may also have been constructed around this time, or may even pre-date the statue.
description_ne: पाटन दरवार क्षेत्रको उत्तरमा रहेको बहादुर शाह भवन (हाल आदर्श कन्या विद्यालय रहेको भवन) सँगै उत्तरतिर जोडिएर रहेको घर नै मूछेँ आगम हो । पहिले मणिगल क्षेत्रमा रहेको घर भन्ने अर्थमा यसलाई 'मणिछेँ' भनिन्थ्यो । सोही 'मणिछेँ' अपभ्रंश भई 'मूछेँ' भएको हो । हेर्दा सामान्य निवासस्थान जस्तो देखिएपनि यो घर तान्त्रिक पूजास्थल (आगम) को रूपमा प्रयोग गरिन्छ । यो बखुम्बाहालका जोशी र ओमबाहालका किसि (श्रेष्ठ)हरूको आगमघर हो । स्वँथ टोलका राजोपाध्यायहरूले यस आगमघरमा नित्यपूजा गर्छन् । तलेजुलाई काठमाडौँमा ल्याउनुभन्दा अघिदेखि पूजा गरिँदै आइरहेको मनमानेश्वरीलाई पनि यसै घरभित्र राखी पूजा गरिँदै आइएको छ ।यस आगमघरभित्र राजाहरूको खड्ग संकलन गरेर राखिएको छ । कुनै गद्दीनशीन राजाको मृत्यु भएपछि उनले प्रयोग गर्ने खड्गलाई यस आगमघरमा सुरक्षित गरी राखिन्छ । हाल यहाँ ३० वटाभन्दा बढी खड्ग संग्रह गरी राखिएका छन् (Jośī 2065, 16-17) ।विसं २०७२ सालको भूकम्पले भुइँतलाको केही अंश मात्र बाँकी हुने गरी यो आगमघर पूरै भत्केको छ । मुख्य आगमदेवीलाई सँगै रहेको घरमा सारिएको छ भने अन्य स-साना देवतालाई पाटन संग्रहालयभित्र सुरक्षित राखिएको छ । भूकम्पअघि यो घर तीन तलाको थियो । घरभित्र पस्ने मुख्य द्वारमा कलात्मक ढंगले निर्मित काठको ढोका राखिएको थियो भने दायाँ-बायाँ स-साना झ्यालमा गणेश र नागकन्या राखिएका थिए । घरको पहिलो र दोस्रो तलामा पासुखाझ्याल थियो । घरको छाना झिँगटीले छाई गजुर राखिएको थियो ।यो आगमघर कहिले बन्यो भन्ने स्पष्ट पार्ने ऐतिहासिक प्रमाण भेटिएको छैन । यो घरको नजिकै उत्तर-पश्चिममा रहेको गणेशको मूर्ति नेसं ५५८ मा स्थापना गरिएकोले त्यसभन्दा पहिले नै यो घर बनिसकेको अनुमान गर्न सकिन्छ।

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of guṭhī and donation of finial and window
historical_events.event_description: A fire worshipping ritual was organised in the Mūchẽ Āgama. Land was donated to fund the establishment of a Busādhãguṭhī.The pinnacle, flags and golden windows were also offered to the deity on this day. The inscription mentions that avarṣavardhana pūjāof theāgamamust be performed every year on the 14th day of the dark half of Vaiśākha. Specific directions regarding the management of the worship for Buṅgabhaṭṭāraka (Rāto Matsyendranātha), Cābuṅgabhaṭṭāraka (Mīnanātha), Paśupatinātha, Guhyeśvarī and Garuḍa Nārāyana are written in the inscription.Actor: Pātravaṃśa Gaṅgāśaṅkara Rāut

historical_events.event_name: Installation of the statue of Gaṇeśa
historical_events.event_description: The stone image of Gaṇeśa was established by Jagatvarddhana Bhāro and Ulhāsavarddhana Bhāro.

On the 6th day of the bright half of Āśvina NS 772, Jyotinarasiṃha Malla (the second son of king Siddhinarasiṃha Malla/younger brother of Śrīnivāsa Malla) died. His wife Chatramatī followed her husband into death and became asatī. The Navarātra of Daśaĩ had been organised to take place that year. Only the royal Upādhyāya priests performed the rituals for ten days. The Taleju was not brought down, and the buffaloes were not sacrificed. Only the deity of Maḍiche (Maṇichẽ) was brought downstairs to the ground floor and placed there according to the tradition. A buffalo was sacrificed at Thaṃchemaṇḍala (Mahālakṣmī) later on. Neither the dance with buffalo-heads was performed nor were the musical instruments played.
The building collapsed in the 1934 CE earthquake.
